analysis: Examined CBv2StageKVHost.swift base vs head. The Gemma 4 branch of init(model:) was refactored into a private static helper gemma4Parts(...) and a new init(gemma4Geometry:...) was added for tensor-parallel ranks. I compared the extracted logic line by line with the base (lines 127-162 base vs head 127-136, 235-267): the page-size computation (pagedRequestBytes, max(kvCapacityBytes, pages) for native, pages for packed), the capacity sum with checked arithmetic, the paged/contiguous switch, the cache count and kind validation, and the nativeRecentBytes call are all unchanged. The new init repeats the same bounds checks (lanes 1...8, maximumTokensPerRequest <= wireContextTokens, maximumChunkTokens > 0). It also requires geometry.host == nil and an empty recurrent layer list, and it keeps the contiguous-requires-native-quantization refusal. No security-relevant check is dropped. Overflow-checked byte arithmetic is retained. The KV pool is per-process in-memory and unshared. The change adds no prefix-cache persistence, no network or wire surface, no key handling and no logging beyond the existing size-only report line. The test file (Gemma4TensorParallelPrefixTests.swift, added) was not supplied as text, only a truncated patch excerpt. It references a Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix with a sealed vote and an encrypted SSD tier that are not in this batch. Those prefix and SSD cache implementations (relevant to T-041 and A-001: cross-tenant scoping, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, sealed vote) cannot be assessed from the supplied evidence and need review wherever they are implemented. The host refactor itself shows no regression.
